U_Y := X minus Y is a smooth open of dimension 21; restriction r : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, both sides have weights at least 26, and r_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) is the induced map of pure weight -16 Hodge structures (CLM-0120-3). T_Z := K_Z := ker(r_T) is a subobject of T, with phi the inclusion (CLM-0120-4). Every class in T supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y lies in T_Z (CLM-0120-5). The datum uses no Tate assertion, no Gysin map, no closed embedding of Z, and no support-exhaustion (CLM-0120-7). Nothing below uses a dimension, purity, irreducibility, regular-immersion, or lci property of Y, nor any map from the cohomology of Z to T.\n\nStandard inputs, already in the register of ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3 as confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170.\n\n(S1) Mixed Hodge structures on ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks over C, functorial for open immersions. For such a stack V, H^m(V; Q) has weights at least m.\n\n(S2) Purity for a smooth pair. If V is a smooth separated finite-type DM stack over C of pure dimension D and S is a smooth closed substack of V of pure codimension c, then there is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures\n\n  ... -> H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) -> H^m(V; Q) -> H^m(V minus S; Q) -> ...\n\nobtained from the purity isomorphism H^m_S(V; Q) isomorphic to H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) together with localization for the closed-open pair (S, V minus S). If Y is empty, take N = 0. Now suppose Y^{(j)} is a nonempty reduced closed substack of X, of dimension d_j. Let C_1, ..., C_r be its irreducible components of dimension d_j. For such a stack V, H^m(V; Q) has weights at least m.\n\n(S2) Purity for a smooth pair. If V is a smooth separated finite-type DM stack over C of pure dimension D and S is a smooth closed substack of V of pure codimension c, then there is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures\n\n  ... -> H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) -> H^m(V; Q) -> H^m(V minus S; Q) -> ...\n\nobtained from the purity isomorphism H^m_S(V; Q) isomorphic to H^{m-2c}(S; Q)(-c) together with localization for the closed-open pair (S, V minus S). Existence of an admissible chain, with no dimension bound for Y\n\nLemma 1. Let Y be a reduced closed substack of X. There exist an integer N >= 0 and reduced closed substacks\n\n  Y = Y^{(0)} superset Y^{(1)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty\n\nsuch that, writing S_j := Y^{(j)} minus Y^{(j+1)} and n_j := dim Y^{(j)}, each S_j is smooth of pure dimension n_j, has affine coarse space, and is closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)}, and n_0 > n_1 > ... > n_{N-1} >= 0 whenever N >= 1.\n\nProof. If Y is empty, take N = 0. Now suppose Y^{(j)} is a nonempty reduced closed substack of X, of dimension d_j. Let C_1, ..., C_r be its irreducible components of dimension d_j. In characteristic zero the singular locus of a reduced finite-type DM stack is a proper closed substack. Set\n\n  O := Y^{(j)} minus (the union of components of dimension < d_j, the pairwise intersections C_a cap C_b for a != b, and Sing(Y^{(j)})).\n\nThen O is open in Y^{(j)}, smooth, of pure dimension d_j, and dense in each C_a, with the pieces O cap C_a pairwise disjoint. The coarse space |X| of M_{6,6} is a quasi-projective variety, so the coarse space of the reduced closed substack Y^{(j)} is quasi-projective, and O^c is a locally closed (hence quasi-projective) subscheme of |X|. Choose a nonempty affine open A_a of each (O cap C_a)^c; such opens exist because a quasi-projective variety admits a dense affine open obtained as the complement of a hypersurface in a projective closure, and finitely many prescribed points on distinct components can be avoided. Let A := A_1 disjoint union ... disjoint union A_r, a finite disjoint union of affine schemes, hence affine. Let S_j be the open substack of O lying over A. Then S_j is smooth of pure dimension d_j with affine coarse space, and is dense in each top-dimensional component C_a.\n\nPut Y^{(j+1)} := (Y^{(j)} minus S_j)_{red}. This is closed in Y^{(j)}, hence closed in X. It is the union of the lower-dimensional components of Y^{(j)} with the sets C_a minus S_j, each a proper closed subset of the irreducible C_a, so dim Y^{(j+1)} <= d_j - 1. Finally S_j = Y^{(j)} cap (X minus Y^{(j+1)}) is closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)} because Y^{(j)} is closed in X. Strict decrease of a nonnegative integer dimension forces termination at the empty stack after finitely many steps. No upper bound on dim Y is used: the only comparison is dim Y^{(j)} <= dim X = 21, which is automatic for a closed substack. This is (i).\n\nBecause the n_j strictly decrease, each integer occurs as a stratum dimension at most once.\n\nAffineness of S_j is constructed by choosing an affine open of a quasi-projective coarse space. The archive constraint that an open subset of an affine stack is automatically affine is not used.\n\n## 2. The support filtration and its graded pieces, for every admissible chain\n\nFix an arbitrary admissible chain as in Lemma 1 (or any other admissible chain: the arguments of this section and the next use only the defining properties). Write V_j := X minus Y^{(j)}. Each V_j is open in X, hence smooth of pure dimension 21. Then V_0 = U_Y, V_N = X, V_j is contained in V_{j+1}, and V_{j+1} minus S_j = V_j. Each A_j is a kernel of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures out of the pure object T, hence a sub-Hodge structure of T, pure polarizable of weight -16.\n\nA_0 = T_Z by CLM-0120-4, because V_0 = U_Y and the map is r_T. A_N = 0, because V_N = X and the restriction is the identity on T. If j increases then V_j enlarges, so restriction to V_j factors through restriction to V_{j+1}, and therefore A_{j+1} is contained in A_j. This is a finite decreasing filtration of T by sub-Hodge structures with A_0 = T_Z and A_N = 0.\n\nLemma 2. For each j, the graded piece A_j / A_{j+1} is a subquotient of the pure polarizable weight -16 Hodge structure W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(n_j).\n\nProof. Apply (S2) to the smooth ambient V_{j+1} of pure dimension 21 and its smooth closed substack S_j of pure dimension n_j, hence of pure codimension c_j := 21 - n_j, at cohomological degree m = 26. The identity m - 2 c_j = 26 - 2(21 - n_j) = 2 n_j - 16 holds, so exactness at H^{26}(V_{j+1}) gives\n\n  ker( H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) -> H^{26}(V_j; Q) ) = image( H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) -> H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) ).\n\nBy (S5) the functor W_{26} is exact, so\n\n  ker( W_{26} H^{26}(V_{j+1}; Q) -> W_{26} H^{26}(V_j; Q) )\n\nequals W_{26} of that image, which is a quotient of W_{26}( H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j) ). No identification of a supports group with its image in T is used: every object here is a kernel of an open restriction. Therefore W_{26} of it equals W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(-c_j). The further twist (21) uses (-c_j) + 21 = n_j, and the resulting weight is (2 n_j - 16) - 2 n_j = -16. This is (ii).\n\nNo Gysin map for the pair (X, Y) or (X, Z), no closed embedding of Z, no fundamental class of Y, no regular immersion of Y, and no degree shift by twice a codimension of Y or Z appears. The only purity sequence is (S2) for the smooth pair constructed in Lemma 1.\n\n## 3. Endpoint vanishings and the dimension-8 piece\n\nLemma 3. With notation as above:\n\n(a) If n_j >= 17, then H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) = 0, hence A_j / A_{j+1} = 0.\n\n(b) If n_j <= 7, then H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q) = 0, hence A_j / A_{j+1} = 0.\n\n(c) If n_j = 8, then W_{2 n_j - 16} H^{2 n_j - 16}(S_j; Q)(n_j) = H^0(S_j; Q)(8), which is a finite direct sum of Q(8), and therefore so is A_j / A_{j+1}.\n\nProof. (a) For n_j >= 17 one has 2 n_j - 16 = n_j + (n_j - 16) >= n_j + 1 > n_j = dim S_j. The group H^0(S_j; Q) of a nonempty finite-type DM stack is Q to the power of the finite set of connected components, pure of weight 0, so W_0 H^0 = H^0. Twisting by (8) yields a finite direct sum of Q(8). By Lemma 2 the graded piece is a subquotient of that group, hence itself a finite direct sum of Q(8) by (S6). If S_j is empty this index does not occur.\n\nThese are the two vanishings and the n_j = 8 Tate statement required by (iii). For every admissible chain, T_Z is isomorphic, not necessarily canonically, to the direct sum of the graded pieces A_j / A_{j+1} indexed by those j with n_j in {8, ..., 16}. At most one such piece occurs per dimension, so at most eight pieces lie in the range 9 <= n_j <= 16.\n\nProof. Each A_j is a subobject of the pure polarizable weight -16 structure T, so the finite filtration T_Z = A_0 superset A_1 superset ... superset A_N = 0 is a filtration by objects of that semisimple abelian category (S6). Semisimplicity supplies some (not unique, not canonical) splitting T_Z isomorphic to the direct sum over j of A_j / A_{j+1}. Lemma 3 kills every summand with n_j <= 7 or n_j >= 17, and identifies the n_j = 8 summand as a finite direct sum of Q(8). The surviving indices therefore lie in {8, ..., 16}. Strict decrease of the n_j in Lemma 1 gives at most one stratum per dimension, hence at most nine surviving dimensions of which at most eight lie in {9, ..., 16}. This is (iv).\n\nT_Z depends only on the pair (X, Y) by CLM-0120-6, so the isomorphism type of the left-hand side is independent of the chain. The individual residual strata S_j with 9 <= n_j <= 16 may depend on the chain; that dependence is outside the scope of this theorem and is not recorded as a defect. No preferred chain is singled out. Clauses (ii) through (iv) have been proved for every admissible chain.\n\nNo realization of any adjudicated non-Tate model as a single admissible stratum is claimed. A proper support is not affine, hence is not an admissible stratum in the sense of Lemma 1; an admissible chain would peel an affine open and leave a lower-dimensional complement. In particular this argument does not present a proper abelian variety (or any other proper non-Tate variety) as a single S_j.\n\n## 5. The sufficiency implication\n\nLemma 5. If for some admissible chain every graded piece A_j / A_{j+1} with 9 <= n_j <= 16 is a finite direct sum of Q(8), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). This is (v), proved as an implication. 2	  "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, conventions, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, after base change to C so that Betti mixed Hodge structures are defined. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of dimension d = 21. The target\n\nT := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincar\u00e9 duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001). In particular H^{26}(X; Q) is mixed of weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26, and T is pure of weight -16. Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist (established fact). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m is an exact functor.\n\nThe mixed Hodge theory used below is exactly the Q-coefficient theory already employed to name T on the smooth stack X and on its open substacks: ordinary cohomology of a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, and the restriction map along an open immersion of such stacks. Compactly supported cohomology of a possibly singular closed substack is not used as a standalone input.\n\nCasnati-Ekedahl conventions, (CE)+(N)+(BAL), H = H_{4,6}(P^1), and H^bal = {F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)} are as in ATT-0112. No global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 is used. No blocked route is used. In particular this argument never invokes vcd-only vanishing, the undecorated top-weight graph complex, a point count, or the forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. Gysin maps, a closed embedding of the reduced-support model itself into X, support-exhaustion, and a monomorphism f: Z -> X are not assumed; the only map to T that is used is constructed in Section 5 from restriction of ordinary cohomology.\n\n## 1. Source geometry (imported from ATT-0112)\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1 and CLM-0112-2, H is a finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 18, and H^bal is open in H, hence itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and CLM-0112-7, every nonempty connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], smooth of pure dimension 15) contains a type-(i) point.\n\nLet V be a finite-type k-scheme with a smooth surjective morphism V -> H^bal (a smooth atlas; H^bal of finite type supplies a finite-type atlas). Let V_beta be any connected component. ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8, over this reduced locally Noetherian scheme, supplies:\n\n- pi_* L locally free of rank three and AJ = P_{V_beta}(pi_* L) a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle;\n- U_beta the distinct-support (reduced-support) open of AJ, V_beta-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective;\n- Z_beta = Ord(U_beta) -> U_beta the finite \u00e9tale right S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal degree-six divisor, of degree 720;\n- Z_beta equal to the CE evaluation-failure model (via the dual-confirmed identifications recorded in ATT-0112 clause (E): ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6).\n\nIn particular Z_beta is a smooth finite-type k-scheme. The reduced-support condition and the ordering are applied to the same scheme; no one-sided reduction is used. Grauert is used only over the reduced scheme V_beta.\n\nWrite Z for the disjoint union of the Z_beta as V_beta runs over connected components of a chosen atlas, or equivalently for any single Z_beta when only geometric points of the image are at issue. Nothing below uses a component formula over a stack with inertia (FND-0144).\n\n## 2. The classifying morphism (constructed, not assumed)\n\nOver Z_beta the pullback of the universal curve of AJ is a smooth proper family C_{Z_beta} -> Z_beta of geometrically connected genus-six curves, equipped with six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 whose relative Cartier divisor is the universal reduced member of |L|. This is precisely an object of the fibre category X(Z_beta). By the 2-Yoneda description of the moduli stack, this object is a morphism of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks\n\nf_beta : Z_beta -> X = M_{6,6}.\n\nNo comparison of Aut(C, gamma, Gamma) with Aut(C, Gamma) is used: existence of f_beta is the universal property of X, which classifies marked curves and does not see the pencil. No claim that f_beta is a monomorphism, unramified, quasi-finite, representable in any stronger sense than a morphism from a scheme to a Deligne-Mumford stack, or a closed immersion, is made. (The blocked monomorphism-without-pencil-recovery route is therefore not taken; pencil recovery is not needed for existence.)\n\nGeometrically, a geometric point of the image is an ordered six-pointed smooth genus-six curve (C, p_1, ..., p_6) for which the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(p_1+...+p_6) is isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal cover (C, gamma) presenting that point of H^bal. This is a description of geometric points of the image, not a stack-level full-faithfulness statement.\n\n## 3. Atlas-independent closed support Y\n\nThe morphism f_beta is of finite type (source and target are). The set-theoretic image of a finite-type morphism of algebraic stacks locally of finite type over a field is a constructible subset of the Zariski topological space of geometric points (Chevalley for algebraic stacks). Let Im be the union of the geometric images of all f_beta for the connected components of a fixed atlas. Let |Y| be the Zariski closure of Im in |X|, and let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X with underlying space |Y|. The closed immersion i: Y -> X exists by this definition of Y; it is not a closed embedding of Z_beta, and it is not asserted to be a regular immersion, lci, or of pure codimension four.\n\nAtlas independence. Let V -> H^bal and V' -> H^bal be two smooth finite-type atlases, with associated images Im and Im'. The fibre product W = V times_{H^bal} V' is again a smooth atlas, and the tautological families on Z_W pull back from both sides, so the classifying morphisms commute with the projections Z_W -> Z_V and Z_W -> Z_{V'}. Smooth (in particular, surjective on geometric points) pullback therefore yields Im = Im_W = Im'. Equivalently, a geometric point of H^bal is an isomorphism class of (C, gamma), and a geometric point of Z is an ordering of a reduced member of |L|; both are intrinsic to the moduli problem and independent of presentation. Hence Y, as the reduced closure of that intrinsic set of geometric points of X, is independent of the atlas.\n\nThe same Y is obtained if one starts from an \u00e9tale atlas of Hbar^bal = [H^bal / PGL_2]: precomposition of gamma with an automorphism of the target replaces D by a linearly equivalent divisor in the same pencil, so (C, Gamma) in X is PGL_2-invariant (ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7). The geometric image in X is therefore unchanged.\n\nY is nonempty: H^bal is nonempty (imported in ATT-0112 from FND-0154), and on every balanced geometric fibre the reduced-support open is nonempty (ATT-0112 clause (E) via ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5, CLM-0088-8). Nonemptiness of Y is recorded only to make the construction non-vacuous; vanishing of T_Z is not excluded and is not needed.\n\n## 4. Localization sequence for X along Y\n\nLet U_Y := X \\ Y, an open substack of the smooth stack X, hence itself smooth of dimension 21. Open-closed decomposition supplies the localization triangle in the derived category of mixed Hodge complexes on the analytic site of X,\n\nR Gamma_Y(X, Q) -> R Gamma(X, Q) -> R Gamma(U_Y, Q) -> +1,\n\nor equivalently the long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures whose degree-26 fragment contains the restriction morphism of ordinary cohomology\n\nr : H^{26}(X; Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y; Q).\n\nThis is a localization sequence for X = M_{6,6}, constructed from the closed-open pair (Y, U_Y). Both X and U_Y are smooth of dimension 21, so H^{26}(X; Q) and H^{26}(U_Y; Q) have weights at least 26, and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} on each. Strictness yields that\n\nGr^W_{26} r : Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) -> Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)\n\nis a morphism of pure polarizable Hodge structures of weight 26. Twisting by (21) and applying the Poincar\u00e9 identification of T gives a morphism of pure weight -16 Hodge structures\n\nr_T : T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nNo Gysin morphism, no fundamental class of Y, and no degree shift by twice the codimension appear. The map r_T is restriction of ordinary cohomology, which exists for an arbitrary open immersion of smooth stacks and does not require Y to be regularly immersed.\n\n(If one prefers the language of cohomology with supports, ker(r) = im(H^{26}_Y(X; Q) -> H^{26}(X; Q)), so the kernel constructed below is exactly the image of the supports map in the sense of FND-0168(3a), once the closed support Y containing the image of Z has been fixed. The kernel itself is named without treating H_c^*(Y) as a standalone theory.)\n\n## 5. The datum (K_Z, T_Z, phi)\n\nDefine\n\nK_Z := ker(r_T) = ker( T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21) ),\n\nT_Z := K_Z,\n\nphi : K_Z -> T the inclusion of this kernel.\n\nThen:\n\n- K_Z is a named mixed Hodge structure: it is the kernel of W_{26} of restriction in the localization sequence of Section 4 for M_{6,6}. Equivalently it is W_{26} of the degree-26 supports group H^{26}_Y(X; Q), twisted by (21). Degree, weight, and twist are those of T: Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, ordinary cohomological degree 26 with Poincar\u00e9 twist (21). No Tate type is asserted.\n- phi is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures, constructed as W_{26}(21) of the restriction map r of Section 4 (or as the supports-to-ambient map). It is not assumed; it is this restriction/kernel inclusion.\n- T_Z is the kernel of r_T, hence a subobject of T, hence a specified subquotient of T. Exactness of Gr^W_{26} on the localization sequence at H^{26}(X) says precisely that T_Z consists of those classes in T whose restriction to U_Y vanishes in W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y; Q)(21).\n\nThis is the CE support-accounting datum attached to the ordered reduced-support evaluation-failure geometry, via the closed support Y constructed from that geometry in Sections 2-3.\n\n## 6. Coverage: no relevant Z-supported term is omitted\n\nBy construction of Y, every geometric point of the image of f_beta lies in Y, so the image of Z is contained in Y and U_Y is disjoint from that image.   "argument_markdown": "## 0. Scope, conventions, and excluded routes\n\nWork throughout with Q-coefficients. Geometry is that of ATT-0112 (C66-GEO-COMP; dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, after base change to C so that Betti mixed Hodge structures are defined. Write X := M_{6,6} for the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of dimension d = 21. The target\n\nT := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X; Q)\n\nis identified with W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q)(21) by Poincar\u00e9 duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001). In particular H^{26}(X; Q) is mixed of weights at least 26, so W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) = Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(X; Q) is a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 26, and T is pure of weight -16. Borel-Moore homology is dual to compactly supported cohomology in the same degree with no extra Tate twist (established fact). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, so Gr^W_m is an exact functor.\n\nThe mixed Hodge theory used below is exactly the Q-coefficient theory already employed to name T on the smooth stack X and on its open substacks: ordinary cohomology of a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, and the restriction map along an open immersion of such stacks. Compactly supported cohomology of a possibly singular closed substack is not used as a standalone input.\n\nCasnati-Ekedahl conventions, (CE)+(N)+(BAL), H = H_{4,6}(P^1), and H^bal = {F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5)} are as in ATT-0112. No global splitting W = W_4 + W_5 is used. No blocked route is used. In particular this argument never invokes vcd-only vanishing, the undecorated top-weight graph complex, a point count, or the forgetful map X -> M_{6,5}. Gysin maps, a closed embedding of the reduced-support model itself into X, support-exhaustion, and a monomorphism f: Z -> X are not assumed; the only map to T that is used is constructed in Section 5 from restriction of ordinary cohomology.\n\n## 1. Source geometry (imported from ATT-0112)\n\nBy ATT-0112/CLM-0112-1 and CLM-0112-2, H is a finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack, smooth of pure dimension 18, and H^bal is open in H, hence itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal. By ATT-0112/CLM-0112-6 and CLM-0112-7, every nonempty connected component of H^bal (and of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2], smooth of pure dimension 15) contains a type-(i) point.\n\nLet V be a finite-type k-scheme with a smooth surjective morphism V -> H^bal (a smooth atlas; H^bal of finite type supplies a finite-type atlas). Let V_beta be any connected component. ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8, over this reduced locally Noetherian scheme, supplies:\n\n- pi_* L locally free of rank three and AJ = P_{V_beta}(pi_* L) a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle;\n- U_beta the distinct-support (reduced-support) open of AJ, V_beta-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective;\n- Z_beta = Ord(U_beta) -> U_beta the finite \u00e9tale right S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal degree-six divisor, of degree 720;\n- Z_beta equal to the CE evaluation-failure model (via the dual-confirmed identifications recorded in ATT-0112 clause (E): ATT-0065/CLM-0065-9 and ATT-0066/CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6).\n\nIn particular Z_beta is a smooth finite-type k-scheme. The reduced-support condition and the ordering are applied to the same scheme; no one-sided reduction is used. Grauert is used only over the reduced scheme V_beta.\n\nWrite Z for the disjoint union of the Z_beta as V_beta runs over connected components of a chosen atlas, or equivalently for any single Z_beta when only geometric points of the image are at issue. The classifying morphism (constructed, not assumed)\n\nOver Z_beta the pullback of the universal curve of AJ is a smooth proper family C_{Z_beta} -> Z_beta of geometrically connected genus-six curves, equipped with six tautological pairwise-disjoint sections sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 whose relative Cartier divisor is the universal reduced member of |L|. This is precisely an object of the fibre category X(Z_beta). By the 2-Yoneda description of the moduli stack, this object is a morphism of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks\n\nf_beta : Z_beta -> X = M_{6,6}.\n\nNo comparison of Aut(C, gamma, Gamma) with Aut(C, Gamma) is used: existence of f_beta is the universal property of X, which classifies marked curves and does not see the pencil. No claim that f_beta is a monomorphism, unramified, quasi-finite, representable in any stronger sense than a morphism from a scheme to a Deligne-Mumford stack, or a closed immersion, is made. Let Im be the union of the geometric images of all f_beta for the connected components of a fixed atlas. Degree, weight, and twist are those of T: Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, ordinary cohomological degree 26 with Poincar\u00e9 twist (21). Let Im subset |M_{6,6}| be the set-theoretic image of the classifying morphism to M_{6,6} of the ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure model of ATT-0112 clause (E). Let Y subseteq Y' be closed substacks of M_{6,6} with Im subset |Y|. Write U := M_{6,6} minus Y and U' := M_{6,6} minus Y', so U' subseteq U are smooth open substacks of dimension 21. The tautological family on Z_W is then the pullback of the families on Z_V and Z_{V'}, so the geometric images of f_V, f_{V'}, and f_W in |X| coincide. Let X denote the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6} of dimension 21, and let T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified by FND-0001 with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21). Let Y be any closed substack of X, write U:=X minus Y, and let T_Z:=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(U;Q)(21)) be the associated kernel-form term (the ATT-0120/FND-0180 interface when Y is the reduced classifying-image closure). Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient identifies cohomology with supports along Y with Borel-Moore homology of Y: topologically H^{BM}_k(Y) isomorphic to H^{2d-k}(X,U) for the closed embedding of Y into the oriented real 2d-manifold underlying X (Iversen IX.4.7), and algebraically H^{26}_Y(X;Q) isomorphic to H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)(21). This identification requires no closed regular embedding of Y, no lci or purity-of-codimension hypothesis, no Gysin map, and no degree shift by twice a codimension. FND-0180 already records that the same duality intertwines ordinary open restriction with Borel-Moore corestriction, so T_Z equals the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T in the sense of FND-0168(3a). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, hence W_{-16} is exact on the Borel-Moore localization sequence, and T_Z is a quotient of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q). Duality convention as in FND-0165: H^{BM}_k(-;Q):=Hom(H_c^k(-;Q),Q) with no extra Tate twist. Deligne's weight bound, recorded for Borel-Moore homology by Hanamura-Saito, gives that H_c^k has weights at most k and therefore H^{BM}_k has weights at least -k, so the bottom step W_{-k}H^{BM}_k is pure of weight -k. Over C this piece is polarizable (graded-polarizable Deligne mixed Hodge structures, including the simplicial-scheme formalism of Hodge III 8.3 applied to an etale atlas of the finite-type stack Y). Thus W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16. Polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033), so a quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is a finite direct sum of Q(8). Hence, for any such Y and in particular for the ATT-0120 support, the condition that W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8) is sufficient for T_Z to be a finite direct sum of Q(8), which is the C66-TATE-SUPPORT conclusion. The condition is sufficient, not necessary: non-Tate summands of the source may die in the map to T. The statement does not assert that the source is Tate, does not prove T_Z Tate, and says nothing about support-exhaustion T_Z=T. Stack-level compactly supported cohomology of Y is used only through the Poincare-Verdier mixed Hodge structure already granted by FND-0180 on the smooth pair (X,U); this does not reopen the FND-0165 exclusion of an independent stack-level H_c formalism. FND-0052 and FND-0168(5a)/(5b) remain binding for any Gysin-style computation that would identify the supports group with a codimension shift of ordinary cohomology of Y, but they are not required for this sufficiency.

**What this artifact does and does not do.** It does not prove the assigned theorem. Three findings made that clear before I started drafting: FND-0191 shows purity + weight + closed support in a smooth 21-fold cannot force Tate type, so real geometric input on the strata is required; FND-0188/FND-0189 rule out any conditional whose antecedent is RED-0001 or an open gap; and the 15 prior attempts on this subproblem all stalled at the same 9–16 range.

**The new content is a change of support.** ATT-0120's `Y` is a Zariski closure — the CE geometry describes its image, nothing describes the boundary. I replace it with `Ŷ := (rk φ ≤ 4)`, the determinantal locus of the canonical evaluation map from the Hodge bundle to the six marked fibres, whose points are exactly those with `h⁰(O_C(Γ)) ≥ 3`. Since `Y ⊆ Ŷ` and kernel-form terms grow with the support, `T_Z ⊆ K(Ŷ)` — so `K(Ŷ)` Tate suffices, and the obligation now sits on an intrinsic locus instead of an unknown boundary.

**A by-product is `dim Y ≤ 17`,** which FND-0194 records as computed by no verified artifact and which REV-0171/REV-0174 rejected in ATT-0121/ATT-0122. The proof runs through the Kempf cover `D ⊂ Gr(2,E)`: its points are pencils of canonical divisors whose base divisor contains Γ, the residual base-point-free pencil has degree 2, 3, or 4, and Riemann-existence + Clifford bound those three strata by 15, 16, 17. It never leaves `M_{6,6}` — no Hbar^bal atlas, no Brauer class, no PGL₂ count — so it sidesteps both repairs FND-0187 left unwritten.

**What remains open** is GAP-0133-1: the Tate type of `K(Ŷ)`. I flag one concrete reason for caution — the `k=2` stratum consists of hyperelliptic curves with six of eight preimages of a degree-four divisor, and the associated configuration-space covers are Kummer-type, exactly the shape of the recorded non-Tate witnesses in FND-0169/FND-0178. Those are model-level classes that FND-0186 shows die in the target, so they are neither inputs nor a disproof here, but they do explain why the "finite cover of a mixed-Tate base" inference is blocked rather than merely unlicensed. ## 0. Scope: what is proved and what is not

The assigned theorem is the unconditional statement that the named subquotient T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). **This artifact does not prove it, and does not disprove it.** What is proved unconditionally is a strictly weaker package (Sections 1-4) which replaces the one object in the assigned setup that no verified artifact describes -- the Zariski closure Y of the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying image -- by an intrinsic, closed, explicitly stratified substack of M_{6,6} containing it, and which as a by-product proves dim Y <= 17. Section 5 states the surviving obligation exactly. No conditional statement is offered in place of the theorem, and no antecedent equivalent to RED-0001 is invoked anywhere (cf. FND-0188, FND-0189).

Work over C with Q-coefficients. Write X := M_{6,6}, the smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of pure dimension d = 3*6-3+6 = 21, with finite inertia and quasi-projective coarse space. By Poincare duality (established working-context fact; packet FND-0001),

  T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21),

which is pure polarizable of weight -16 because X is smooth, so H^{26}(X;Q) has weights at least 26 and W_{26} = Gr^W_{26} there; the arithmetic is 2*21-16 = 26 and 26-2*21 = -16.

### 0.1 Verified inputs actually used

From the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE attempt **ATT-0120** (dual-confirmed by REV-0169 and REV-0170) I use only: CLM-0120-2 (Y is an atlas-independent reduced closed substack of X, namely the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image of the classifying morphism f from the ordered reduced-support balanced CE model, whose geometric points are the (C,p_1,...,p_6) with p_i pairwise distinct and O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to L on a balanced tetragonal pair, Gamma := p_1 + ... + p_6); CLM-0120-3 (U_Y := X minus Y is smooth of dimension 21 and r_T : T -> W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21) is W_{26} of ordinary open restriction, twisted by (21)); CLM-0120-4 (T_Z := ker(r_T) is a subobject of T, phi its inclusion); CLM-0120-5 (one-sided coverage); CLM-0120-6 (the datum depends only on the pair (X,Y)); CLM-0120-7 (no Tate, Gysin, embedding or exhaustion content). No dimension, purity, irreducibility, lci or regular-immersion property of Y is imported: ATT-0120 asserts none.

From the verified C66-SUPPORT-FILTRATION attempt **ATT-0130** (dual-confirmed by REV-0180 and REV-0181) I use CLM-0130-1 through CLM-0130-5: existence of an admissible chain for Y, the kernel filtration A_j := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j)};Q)(21)) with A_0 = T_Z and A_N = 0, the graded-piece bound A_j/A_{j+1} a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j), the endpoint resolution (zero for n_j <= 7 and n_j >= 17, a finite direct sum of Q(8) at n_j = 8), the noncanonical semisimple splitting, and the sufficiency implication.

### 0.2 Established working-context facts used

(E1) On the balanced locus, h^0(O_C(D)) = 2, h^0(L) = 3 and h^1(L) = 2, without fibrewise jumping.
(E2) The relative-canonical normalization gives W_4 = omega_C^2, W_5 = omega_C^2(-D), and L := W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D), with D a divisor of the tetragonal pencil.
(E3) Pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category; every subobject or quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is again a finite direct sum of Q(8) (packet FND-0033).
(E4) Riemann-Roch and Serre duality on smooth projective connected curves, and the Poincare reindexing of Section 0.

### 0.3 Classical source-backed inputs

(C1) *Clifford's theorem.* For a special effective line bundle A on a smooth projective connected curve, h^0(A) <= deg(A)/2 + 1, with equality only for A = O, A = omega, or C hyperelliptic with A a multiple of the g^1_2.
(C2) *Riemann-Hurwitz and Riemann existence.* For a degree-k cover of P^1 by a smooth connected curve of genus g, the total branching is 2g-2+2k; and the stack of degree-k covers with a fixed number m of branch points and fixed local monodromy data is finite etale over the configuration space of the m branch points in P^1.
(C3) *Grassmann bundles.* For a locally free sheaf E of rank r on an algebraic stack X, Gr(2,E) -> X is smooth and proper of relative dimension 2(r-2); a closed substack of Gr(2,E) is therefore proper over X, and the image of a proper morphism is closed with dimension at most that of the source.
(C4) Mixed Hodge structures on ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type DM stacks over C, functorial for open immersions, with H^m of weights at least m; strictness of morphisms for W, hence exactness of W_m.

No virtual cohomological dimension, graph complex, point count, or forgetful map X -> M_{6,5} is used anywhere below.

## 1. The canonical evaluation map and the intrinsic locus Yhat

Let p : C_X -> X be the universal curve, sigma_1, ..., sigma_6 the six marked sections (pairwise disjoint, by definition of M_{6,6}), and put

  E := p_* omega_{C_X/X}   (the Hodge bundle, locally free of rank g = 6),
  F := direct sum over i = 1..6 of sigma_i^* omega_{C_X/X}   (locally free of rank 6),
  phi : E -> F   the evaluation morphism, restriction of a relative canonical form to the six marked sections.

Both E and F are locally free of rank 6 and phi is a morphism of locally free sheaves on X; no base-change or jumping hypothesis is needed, since p_* omega_{C/X} is locally free of rank g with formation commuting with base change for a smooth proper relative curve, and sigma_i^* is exact on locally free sheaves.

**Definition.** Yhat := the reduced closed substack of X supported on the locus where rk(phi) <= 4, i.e. on the vanishing of the ideal of 5-by-5 minors of phi.

**Lemma 1.1 (fibrewise identification).** Let x = (C, p_1, ..., p_6) be a geometric point of X and Gamma := p_1 + ... + p_6, an effective divisor of degree 6 with pairwise distinct support. Then ker(phi_x) = H^0(C, omega_C(-Gamma)) and

  x lies in Yhat  <=>  h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2  <=>  h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3.

*Proof.* A section s of omega_C lies in ker(phi_x) exactly when s(p_i) = 0 for i = 1, ..., 6. Because the p_i are pairwise distinct, Gamma is reduced and this is exactly the condition s in H^0(omega_C(-Gamma)). Hence rk(phi_x) = 6 - h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) and rk(phi_x) <= 4 is equivalent to h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2. For the second equivalence, Serre duality gives h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) = h^1(O_C(Gamma)), and Riemann-Roch gives h^0(O_C(Gamma)) - h^1(O_C(Gamma)) = deg(Gamma) - g + 1 = 6 - 6 + 1 = 1, so h^1(O_C(Gamma)) = h^0(O_C(Gamma)) - 1. Therefore h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2 if and only if h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3. (E4) []

**Lemma 1.2.** Yhat is a closed substack of X, atlas-independent, and its formation commutes with base change to any smooth atlas.

*Proof.* A determinantal locus of a morphism of locally free sheaves is closed and its formation is compatible with pullback, since minors pull back to minors. Reducedness is imposed and is preserved by the unique reduced structure on a closed subset. Atlas independence is immediate because E, F, phi are globally defined on X. []

The generic determinantal expected codimension of (rk <= 4) for a map of rank-6 sheaves is (6-4)(6-4) = 4. **This number is recorded only for orientation. No consequence is drawn from it below**: neither purity of dimension, nor equidimensionality, nor an lci or regular-immersion property of Yhat is claimed or used. The dimension bound in Section 3 is proved independently, exactly as the recorded constraint on expected-codimension bookkeeping demands.

## 2. Y is contained in Yhat, and the resulting comparison of kernel-form terms

**Lemma 2.1.** Y is a closed substack of Yhat.

*Proof.* Let x = (C, p_1, ..., p_6) be a geometric point of the classifying image of ATT-0120/CLM-0120-2. By construction of that image, the p_i are pairwise distinct and O_C(Gamma) is isomorphic to L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} on a balanced tetragonal pair (C, gamma). By (E1) one has h^0(L) = 3 on the balanced locus, hence h^0(O_C(Gamma)) = 3 >= 3, and Lemma 1.1 places x in Yhat.

(Independent cross-check, not needed for the proof: by (E2), L = omega_C(-D) with D a divisor of the pencil gamma, so omega_C(-Gamma) is isomorphic to omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D), and h^0(O_C(D)) >= 2 because D moves in a pencil. This gives h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2 directly, again by Lemma 1.1.)

Thus the geometric image of the classifying morphism is contained in the closed subset |Yhat| of |X|. Its Zariski closure is therefore contained in |Yhat|, and since Y carries the reduced structure on that closure (CLM-0120-2), Y is a closed substack of Yhat. []

For a closed substack V of X set

  K(V) := ker( T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V;Q)(21) ),

the map being W_{26} of ordinary open restriction, twisted by (21). Each K(V) is the kernel of a morphism of mixed Hodge structures out of the pure polarizable weight -16 object T, hence a sub-Hodge structure of T, pure polarizable of weight -16 (C4). By ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4, K(Y) = T_Z.

**Lemma 2.2 (monotonicity).** If V is a closed substack of V', then K(V) is a subobject of K(V'). In particular T_Z = K(Y) is a subobject of K(Yhat).

*Proof.* X minus V' is an open substack of X minus V, so ordinary restriction H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(X minus V';Q) factors as restriction to X minus V followed by restriction to X minus V'. Applying the exact functor W_{26} and twisting by (21) (C4), the map T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V';Q)(21) factors through T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V;Q)(21). A class killed by the first map is therefore killed by the second, i.e. K(V) is contained in K(V'), and both are subobjects of T. Lemma 2.1 gives the last assertion. []

**Corollary 2.3 (Tate transfer).** If K(Yhat) is a finite direct sum of Q(8), then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

*Proof.* T_Z is a subobject of K(Yhat) inside the semisimple abelian category of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight -16, and every subobject of a finite direct sum of Q(8) there is again such a sum (E3). []

This is the structural point of the artifact. The assigned obligation is stated for Y, which is by construction a Zariski closure of a constructible image: the CE geometry describes the image, and nothing in the verified inputs describes the points of Y outside it. Corollary 2.3 legitimately transports the whole obligation onto Yhat, which is defined by a single intrinsic determinantal condition on X and whose geometry is entirely accessible (Section 3). Note the direction: enlarging the support enlarges the kernel-form term, so the sufficient condition obtained is a genuine sufficient condition for the assigned conclusion and not a weakening of it.

## 3. The Kempf cover of Yhat and the bound dim Yhat <= 17

Let Gr(2,E) -> X be the Grassmann bundle of rank-two subsheaves of E, smooth and proper over X of relative dimension 2(6-2) = 8, hence of pure dimension 21 + 8 = 29 (C3). Let S be the tautological rank-two subbundle and let

  D := the zero locus of the induced section of Hom(S, F) = S^dual tensor F (of rank 2*6 = 12),

with its reduced structure; concretely D = ( (x, V) : V a rank-two subspace of E_x with phi_x(V) = 0 ).

**Lemma 3.1.** The projection rho : D -> X is proper with image exactly Yhat; in particular rho : D -> Yhat is proper and surjective and dim Yhat <= dim D.

*Proof.* D is closed in Gr(2,E), which is proper over X, so rho is proper (C3). A geometric point x lies in the image if and only if ker(phi_x) contains a two-dimensional subspace, i.e. if and only if h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, which by Lemma 1.1 is exactly membership in Yhat. Properness makes the image closed, and the image of a morphism has dimension at most that of the source. []

**Lemma 3.2 (structure of a point of D).** A geometric point of D is a triple (C, (p_i), V) where V is a two-dimensional subspace of H^0(C, omega_C) all of whose members vanish on Gamma. Write B := the base (fixed) divisor of the pencil V, b := deg B, A := omega_C(-B), and W := the induced base-point-free pencil of degree k := 10 - b in H^0(A). Then

  (i) Gamma <= B, hence b >= 6 and k <= 4;
  (ii) k >= 2, so k lies in (2,3,4);
  (iii) V is recovered from (A, W, B) as W multiplied by a defining section of B, so (C, (p_i), V) is determined by the pair (C, W) together with B in the complete linear system |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| and the choice of the degree-six subdivisor Gamma of B with an ordering of its support.

*Proof.* (i) Every member of V vanishes on the reduced divisor Gamma, so Gamma is contained in the greatest common divisor B of the divisors of V; degrees give b >= 6, and deg(A) = 10 - b = k <= 4. (ii) W is a base-point-free pencil on C, i.e. a morphism C -> P^1 of degree k; degree 0 is impossible for a pencil and degree 1 would force C rational, contradicting g = 6. (iii) is the definition of the base divisor: V = H^0(B) multiplied into W under H^0(A) tensor H^0(O(B)) -> H^0(omega_C), and Gamma is one of the finitely many degree-six subdivisors of the fixed divisor B whose support consists of six distinct points, of which there are finitely many orderings. []

So D is covered by the finitely many locally closed substacks D_k (k = 2, 3, 4) on which deg Bs(V) = 10 - k is constant. Lemma 3.2(iii) exhibits, on each D_k, a morphism to the moduli of pairs (C, W) with W a base-point-free pencil of degree k, whose fibres are the pairs (B, Gamma with ordering), i.e. |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| together with a finite choice.

**Lemma 3.3 (pencil moduli).** For g = 6 and k in (2,3,4), every irreducible component of the moduli of pairs (C, W) with C smooth connected of genus 6 and W a base-point-free pencil of degree k has dimension at most 2g-2+2k-3 = 7 + 2k, i.e. at most 11, 13, 15 for k = 2, 3, 4 respectively.

*Proof.* W is the same datum as a degree-k morphism C -> P^1 up to the PGL_2-action on the target. By Riemann-Hurwitz the total branching of such a cover is 2g-2+2k = 10+2k, and each branch point contributes at least 1, so the number m of branch points satisfies m <= 10+2k. Stratify by the (finitely many) discrete branching types. By Riemann existence (C2), the stratum with a fixed branching type is finite etale over the configuration space of its m branch points in P^1, hence has dimension m. Since m >= 3 (the total branching 10+2k >= 14 is distributed among points each of local contribution at most k-1 <= 3, so m >= 5), PGL_2 acts with finite stabilizers on each such configuration and the quotient has dimension m - 3 <= 10+2k-3 = 7+2k. Every component of the moduli of pairs lies in the closure of one such stratum, so the bound holds componentwise. []

**Proposition 3.4.** dim D <= 17. More precisely dim D_2 <= 15, dim D_3 <= 16, dim D_4 <= 17.

*Proof.* Fix k and work on D_k. By Lemma 3.2(iii), dim D_k <= dim (moduli of (C,W) of degree k) + max over such (C,W) of dim |omega_C tensor A^{-1}|, the residual finite choices contributing nothing. By Riemann-Roch and Serre duality,

  dim |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| = h^0(omega_C tensor A^{-1}) - 1 = h^1(A) - 1 = h^0(A) - deg(A) + g - 1 - 1 = h^0(A) - k + 4.

Now bound h^0(A) for deg(A) = k <= 4 on a genus-six curve. A is special (h^1(A) = h^0(omega tensor A^{-1}) >= 1 since deg(omega tensor A^{-1}) = 10-k >= 6 > 0 and, more simply, h^1(A) = h^0(A)-k+5 >= 2-4+5 > 0), so Clifford (C1) gives h^0(A) <= k/2 + 1, with equality only in the excluded cases A = O, A = omega, or C hyperelliptic with A a multiple of the g^1_2.

- k = 2: h^0(A) <= 2, and h^0(A) = 2 exactly for a g^1_2. So h^0(A) = 2, the fibre dimension is 2-2+4 = 4, and by Lemma 3.3, dim D_2 <= 11 + 4 = 15.
- k = 3: Clifford gives h^0(A) <= 3/2 + 1 = 2.5, hence h^0(A) = 2, fibre dimension 2-3+4 = 3, and dim D_3 <= 13 + 3 = 16.
- k = 4: Clifford gives h^0(A) <= 3. If h^0(A) = 2 the fibre dimension is 2, and Lemma 3.3 gives dim <= 15 + 2 = 17. If h^0(A) = 3, Clifford equality with deg(A) = 4 not in (0, 2g-2) forces C hyperelliptic and A = twice the g^1_2; then the pairs (C,W) of this type form a family of dimension at most (dimension of the hyperelliptic locus) + dim Gr(2, H^0(A)) = 11 + dim Gr(2,3) = 11 + 2 = 13, while the fibre dimension is 3-4+4 = 3, giving at most 13 + 3 = 16. (The hyperelliptic locus has dimension 2g-1 = 11, which is the k = 2 case of Lemma 3.3.)

Taking the maximum, dim D <= 17. []

**Corollary 3.5.** dim Yhat <= 17, and consequently dim Y <= 17.

*Proof.* Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 3.4 give dim Yhat <= dim D <= 17. Lemma 2.1 gives Y contained in Yhat, and a closed substack has dimension at most that of the ambient closed substack. []

**Remark 3.6 (what Corollary 3.5 does and does not do).** FND-0181 proves only dim Y <= 20, from the H^bal-level model of dimension 18+2; FND-0187 records that the two candidate repairs to 17 (a Severi-Brauer relative linear system over an atlas of Hbar^bal, or a PGL_2-quotient factorization) must be written out and are not licensed by citing CLM-0112-8 unchanged; FND-0194 records that no verified artifact computes dim Y. Corollary 3.5 avoids both repairs entirely: it never leaves M_{6,6}, uses no atlas of Hbar^bal, no twisted invertible sheaf, no Brauer class, and no PGL_2-quotient dimension count. It also does not assert equality dim Y = 17, does not assert equidimensionality or purity of Y or Yhat, and does not assert that Yhat has codimension 4 as a scheme-theoretic or lci statement.

**Remark 3.7 (cross-check against the recorded reusable computation).** The archive reusable computation records that a relative P^2 over a 15-dimensional base has dimension 17. That is precisely the k = 4, h^0(A) = 2 case above: the pairs (C, base-point-free g^1_4) form a family of dimension at most 15, and |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| is then a P^2. The present derivation is independent of that record (it is proved from Riemann-Hurwitz, Riemann existence, Riemann-Roch and Clifford) and agrees with it. A second independent route agrees as well: stratifying M_6 by hyperelliptic (dimension 11, dim W^1_4 = 2), trigonal (13), bielliptic (10), plane quintic (12) and the complement (15, where Martens-Mumford give dim W^1_4 = 0), and using Lemma 1.1 with W^2_6 isomorphic to W^1_4 by residuation, gives fibre dimensions 4, 3, 3, 3, 2 and totals 15, 16, 13, 15, 17. I record this only as a consistency check; the proof above does not depend on Martens or Mumford, and **no cohomological conclusion whatever is drawn from any gonality or Brill-Noether stratification** (see Section 6).

## 4. Consequences for the assigned filtration

Fix the verified admissible chain machinery of ATT-0130 for Y. By CLM-0130-1 an admissible chain Y = Y^{(0)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty exists; by CLM-0130-2 the A_j form a finite decreasing filtration of T by sub-Hodge structures with A_0 = T_Z, A_N = 0, and A_j/A_{j+1} a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j); by CLM-0130-3 the piece vanishes for n_j <= 7 and for n_j >= 17 and is a finite direct sum of Q(8) at n_j = 8; by CLM-0130-4 T_Z is noncanonically the direct sum of the pieces with n_j in (8, ..., 16), at most one per dimension.

**Corollary 4.1.** For every admissible chain for Y, n_0 = dim Y <= 17. Hence at most one stratum has dimension >= 17, its graded piece vanishes by CLM-0130-3, and T_Z is isomorphic to the direct sum of the graded pieces with 8 <= n_j <= 16, of which the n_j = 8 piece is a finite direct sum of Q(8) and at most eight lie in the range 9 <= n_j <= 16.

*Proof.* Immediate from Corollary 3.5 and CLM-0130-3, CLM-0130-4. []

Corollary 4.1 sharpens the a priori situation only mildly (the dimensions 18, 19, 20 were already resolved to zero by CLM-0130-3); its value is that it is now proved rather than assumed, and that dim Y is no longer an unknown quantity in the range 0..20. **The residual range 9 <= n <= 16 is not reduced by Corollary 4.1.** It is reduced in a different sense by Corollary 2.3: the eight residual graded pieces of an unknown Zariski closure may be replaced, as a sufficient condition, by a single statement about the intrinsic locus Yhat.

**Corollary 4.2 (the surviving sufficient condition, in intrinsic form).** Suppose K(Yhat) is a finite direct sum of Q(8). Then T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8), i.e. the assigned theorem holds. In particular it suffices to exhibit one chain Yhat = V^{(0)} superset ... superset V^{(M)} = empty of reduced closed substacks of X with strictly decreasing dimensions m_i = dim V^{(i)}, each difference R_i := V^{(i)} minus V^{(i+1)} smooth of pure dimension m_i with affine coarse space and closed in X minus V^{(i+1)}, such that for every i with 9 <= m_i <= 16 the corresponding graded piece of the kernel filtration of K(Yhat) is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

*Proof.* The first sentence is Corollary 2.3. For the second, the proof of CLM-0130-1 through CLM-0130-5 uses about its support only that it is a reduced closed substack of the smooth separated finite-type DM stack X with quasi-projective coarse space; the peeling construction, the purity sequence for each smooth pair (X minus V^{(i+1)}, R_i) in degree 26 and codimension 21 - m_i, the exactness of W_{26}, the smooth weight bound, Artin vanishing on the affine coarse space for m_i >= 17, negativity of 2m_i - 16 for m_i <= 7, and semisimplicity apply verbatim with Yhat in place of Y and K(Yhat) in place of T_Z. By Corollary 3.5, dim Yhat <= 17, so the same endpoint analysis applies. []

## 5. The surviving obligation, stated exactly

What remains open, and is **not** proved here, is:

  (R) K(Yhat) -- equivalently, by Corollary 4.2, every graded piece in dimensions 9 <= m <= 16 of one admissible chain for Yhat -- is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

I record why the material now available does not close (R), so that the gap is auditable rather than decorative.

1. *No purely formal route exists.* FND-0191 exhibits X = A x P^{12} with A an abelian ninefold and Y = A x (point): there W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) maps isomorphically onto a summand H^2(A)(9) of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) of Hodge types (-7,-9), (-8,-8), (-9,-7), which is not a finite direct sum of Q(8). Hence purity, Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, closed support in a smooth 21-fold, and the affine-peeling endpoint analysis cannot suffice; genuine geometric input on the residual strata is required. Sections 1-4 supply geometric input (an intrinsic support of dimension at most 17 with an explicit proper cover D and its trichotomy k in (2,3,4)); they do not supply the cohomological input (R) needs.

2. *Artin vanishing stops exactly at 17.* For a stratum of dimension m with affine coarse space, the graded piece is a subquotient of W_{2m-16}H^{2m-16} of it, and 2m-16 > m precisely when m >= 17. For 9 <= m <= 16 the relevant degree is at most the dimension, so no affineness argument vanishes it. Moreover the lowest-weight group W_r H^r of a smooth affine variety of dimension m need not be Tate for r <= m: for a smooth affine ninefold of the form (abelian surface minus an ample divisor) x A^7, W_2H^2 contains the (2,0)-part of the abelian surface. So an affine-only hypothesis on the residual strata is not enough, independently of which support is used.

3. *The explicit strata of D are exactly the places where non-Tate classes are already known to exist at model level.* The k = 2 stratum of D consists of a hyperelliptic curve, a degree-four divisor on P^1, and six of the eight preimages with an ordering; the associated covers of configuration spaces are Kummer-type, and the packet already records non-Tate witnesses of exactly this shape at the level of the models: FND-0169 and ATT-0118 (mu_3-Kummer cover of M_{0,4}, giving a type (15,1) class in a Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16} of a Hurwitz atlas), ATT-0119 and FND-0178 (a constant family over affine 8-space, giving a type (10,6) class in Gr^W_{16}H_c^{16}(Z;Q) of the CE model). Those are model-level classes; FND-0186 shows that the classifying-image closure of a constant or product model of that kind has dimension at most 2 and hence contributes zero to the kernel-form term, and FND-0170 explicitly declines to assert non-Tateness of the CE model's corner. **They are therefore not disproofs, and I do not present them as such.** They are the reason (R) cannot be settled by asserting that the strata are covers of mixed-Tate configuration spaces: the recorded constraints forbid exactly that inference (Section 6), and the witnesses show the inference is not merely unlicensed but false at model level.

4. *No admissible shortcut through the campaign target.* FND-0188 adjudicates that RED-0001 implies (R) trivially by FND-0033, that this is not a weakest sufficient input, and that assuming it is circular in the campaign DAG; FND-0189 adjudicates that an artifact concluding Tate type only under an undischarged antecedent fails the target-interface contract. Accordingly this artifact states no such conditional as its conclusion and lists (R) as an open gap.

I therefore report the assigned theorem as **not resolved** by this artifact, with (R) recorded as GAP-0133-1.

claims.statement: Let phi: E -> F be the canonical evaluation morphism on X = M_{6,6} from the Hodge bundle E = p_* omega_{C/X} (rank 6) to F = the direct sum of sigma_i^* omega_{C/X} over the six marked sections (rank 6), and let Yhat be the reduced closed substack supported on (rk phi <= 4). Then Yhat is closed and atlas-independent, and for every geometric point (C, p_1, ..., p_6) with Gamma := p_1 + ... + p_6 one has ker(phi) = H^0(omega_C(-Gamma)), so that the point lies in Yhat if and only if h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, equivalently h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3. No purity of dimension, equidimensionality, lci or regular-immersion property is claimed, and no consequence is drawn from the generic determinantal expected codimension 4.

The ATT-0120 support Y is a closed substack of Yhat. Every geometric point of the classifying image has O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to L with h^0(L) = 3 on the balanced locus (established fact), hence h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3; Yhat is closed, so the reduced Zariski closure Y of that image lies in Yhat. An independent cross-check uses L = omega_C(-D) and h^0(O_C(D)) >= 2.

For closed substacks V contained in V' of X, the kernel-form terms K(V) := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus V;Q)(21)) satisfy K(V) contained in K(V') as sub-Hodge structures of T, because restriction to the smaller open factors through restriction to the larger one and W_{26} is exact. In particular T_Z = K(Y) is a subobject of K(Yhat), and since pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of weight -16 form a semisimple abelian category, K(Yhat) being a finite direct sum of Q(8) implies T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8).

Let D be the reduced closed substack of the Grassmann bundle Gr(2,E) over X consisting of pairs (x,V) with V a rank-two subspace of E_x killed by phi_x. Then D is proper over X with image exactly Yhat, and a geometric point of D is a pencil V of canonical divisors whose base divisor B contains Gamma; the moving part of V is a base-point-free pencil of degree k = 10 - deg B, and k lies in (2,3,4).

dim D <= 17, with dim D_k <= 15, 16, 17 for k = 2, 3, 4. The bound uses only: the Riemann-existence dimension count 2g-2+2k-3 for moduli of pairs (curve of genus 6, base-point-free pencil of degree k), the identity dim |omega_C tensor A^{-1}| = h^1(A) - 1 = h^0(A) - k + 4, Clifford's bound h^0(A) <= k/2 + 1 with its equality analysis, and finiteness of the choice of a degree-six subdivisor of B with an ordering. Consequently dim Yhat <= 17 and dim Y <= 17.

For every admissible chain for Y in the sense of ATT-0130, n_0 = dim Y <= 17, so at most one stratum has dimension at least 17 and its graded piece vanishes; T_Z is noncanonically the direct sum of the graded pieces with 8 <= n_j <= 16, the n_j = 8 piece being a finite direct sum of Q(8) and at most eight pieces lying in 9 <= n_j <= 16. Moreover the ATT-0130 peeling, purity, endpoint and semisimplicity arguments apply verbatim to Yhat and K(Yhat), so it suffices for the assigned theorem that every graded piece in dimensions 9 through 16 of one admissible chain for Yhat be a finite direct sum of Q(8). This bound on dim Y is obtained without any atlas of Hbar^bal, twisted invertible sheaf, Brauer class, or PGL_2-quotient count, hence independently of both repairs that FND-0187 leaves unwritten; equality dim Y = 17 is not asserted.

The assigned unconditional conclusion, that the named T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8), is NOT established by this artifact. The surviving obligation is that K(Yhat) be a finite direct sum of Q(8), equivalently that every graded piece in dimensions 9 through 16 of one admissible chain for Yhat be such a sum. No conditional is offered as the theorem, RED-0001 is never assumed, and no non-Tate subquotient of the named T_Z is exhibited, so neither a proof nor a disproof is claimed.

parsed_artifact.summary: Unconditional partial result toward C66-TATE-SUPPORT; the assigned conclusion is NOT reached and the residual gap is recorded. New content: the mysterious Zariski closure Y of ATT-0120 is replaced by an intrinsic closed substack of M_{6,6}. Let phi: E -> F = direct sum of sigma_i^* omega_{C/X} be the canonical evaluation map from the Hodge bundle to the fibres at the six marked sections, and let Yhat := (rk phi <= 4)_red. Then Yhat is closed with geometric points exactly the (C,p_1..p_6) satisfying h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, equivalently h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3, for Gamma = p_1 + ... + p_6. (1) Y is contained in Yhat, because on the balanced locus O_C(Gamma) is isomorphic to L and h^0(L) = 3 (established fact), and Yhat is closed. (2) Since restriction factors through the larger open, T_Z = K(Y) is a sub-Hodge structure of K(Yhat); by semisimplicity of pure polarizable weight -16 structures, K(Yhat) a finite direct sum of Q(8) implies T_Z is one. (3) dim Yhat <= 17, hence dim Y <= 17: the Kempf space D = ((x,V) in Gr(2,E) : phi_x(V) = 0) is proper and surjective onto Yhat, a point of D is a pencil V of canonical divisors whose base divisor contains Gamma, its moving part is a base-point-free pencil of degree k = 10 - deg Bs(V) in {2,3,4}, and the Riemann-existence dimension bound 2g-2+2k-3 for pencils together with dim |omega tensor A^{-1}| = h^1(A) - 1 and Clifford gives dim D_k <= 15, 16, 17 for k = 2, 3, 4. This supplies, by a route independent of the PGL_2/Severi-Brauer repair that FND-0187 left unwritten, the bound FND-0194 records as computed by no verified artifact. What remains open is exactly the Tate type of K(Yhat), equivalently of the residual graded pieces in dimensions 9 to 16; no conditional is presented as the theorem.

target_interface_reference.chain_and_strata: Two chains are in play. (a) The verified chain for Y (ATT-0130/CLM-0130-1): Y = Y^{(0)} superset ... superset Y^{(N)} = empty of reduced closed substacks of X with strictly decreasing dimensions n_j = dim Y^{(j)}, each S_j := Y^{(j)} minus Y^{(j+1)} smooth of pure dimension n_j with affine coarse space and closed in X minus Y^{(j+1)}, giving A_j := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^{(j)};Q)(21)) with A_0 = T_Z, A_N = 0, and A_j/A_{j+1} a subquotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j), zero for n_j <= 7 and n_j >= 17 and a finite direct sum of Q(8) at n_j = 8. This artifact proves in addition that n_0 = dim Y <= 17 (Corollary 3.5), so the top piece vanishes and T_Z is the direct sum of the pieces with 8 <= n_j <= 16, at most eight of them in 9 <= n_j <= 16. (b) The new intrinsic support: Yhat := (rk phi <= 4)_red for the canonical evaluation phi : E -> F, whose geometric points are exactly those with h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3. Yhat is closed and contains Y, dim Yhat <= 17, and Yhat carries a proper surjective Kempf cover D inside Gr(2,E) with the closed three-step filtration by the residual base-point-free pencil degree k in (2,3,4), the strata having dimensions at most 15 (k=2, hyperelliptic), 16 (k=3, trigonal) and 17 (k=4). The ATT-0130 peeling, purity, endpoint and semisimplicity arguments apply verbatim to Yhat, so an admissible chain for Yhat exists with the same endpoint resolution.
target_interface_reference.residual_piece_resolution: NOT RESOLVED, and reported as such. The residual pieces of dimensions 9 <= n <= 16 are not determined here, for either chain: neither W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) nor the corresponding graded piece is computed or shown to vanish for any n in that range. What is achieved is a change of the object the residual obligation is attached to. By monotonicity of kernel-form terms and semisimplicity of pure polarizable weight -16 Hodge structures, T_Z is a subobject of K(Yhat), so it is sufficient to prove that K(Yhat) is a finite direct sum of Q(8) -- equivalently that all residual graded pieces in dimensions 9 through 16 of one admissible chain for the intrinsic Yhat are such sums. That obligation is recorded as GAP-0133-1 and is left open. Section 5 of the argument states why the available mechanisms do not close it: Artin vanishing applies only when 2n-16 > n, i.e. n >= 17; the lowest-weight group W_r H^r of a smooth affine variety of dimension m need not be Tate for r <= m; FND-0191 shows purity plus weight plus closed support in a smooth 21-fold cannot suffice; and the recorded model-level non-Tate witnesses (FND-0169, FND-0178, ATT-0118, ATT-0119) are neither used as inputs nor claimed to survive in T, so they neither close nor refute the obligation. No antecedent equivalent to RED-0001 is assumed in place of the missing step, and no conditional is presented as the theorem.
target_interface_reference.target_map_use: phi is used only as the inclusion of ker(r_T) into T, as constructed in ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3 and CLM-0120-4 from W_{26} of ordinary open restriction twisted by (21). The only new map introduced is the analogous kernel inclusion K(Yhat) -> T for the larger closed support Yhat, formed by the identical construction with X minus Yhat in place of X minus Y; since X minus Yhat is an open substack of X minus Y, restriction factors and T_Z is a subobject of K(Yhat). No Gysin map, no proper pushforward from a model of Y, Yhat, or Z into T, no fundamental class, and no codimension shift for any of them is used. target_interface_reference.target_subquotient: T_Z = K(Y) = ker(r_T), the subobject of T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) defined in ATT-0120/CLM-0120-4 as the kernel of r_T : T -> W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)(21), where Y is the atlas-independent reduced closed substack of ATT-0120/CLM-0120-2. This artifact works with exactly that named subquotient and with no surrogate: every conclusion about T_Z is obtained from T_Z as a subobject of the enlarged kernel-form term K(Yhat) attached to a closed substack Yhat of M_{6,6} that is proved to contain Y.
target_interface_reference.unconditional_conclusion: Proved unconditionally, over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n) = (6,6), with no undischarged antecedent and without assuming RED-0001: (1) the canonical evaluation phi : E -> F on M_{6,6} has determinantal locus Yhat := (rk phi <= 4)_red closed and atlas-independent, with geometric points exactly the (C,p_1,...,p_6) satisfying h^0(omega_C(-Gamma)) >= 2, equivalently h^0(O_C(Gamma)) >= 3, for Gamma = p_1 + ... + p_6; (2) the ATT-0120 support Y is a closed substack of Yhat, because on the balanced locus O_C(Gamma) is isomorphic to L with h^0(L) = 3 and Yhat is closed; (3) consequently T_Z = K(Y) is a sub-Hodge structure of K(Yhat), and K(Yhat) being a finite direct sum of Q(8) implies T_Z is one; (4) the Kempf space D inside Gr(2,E) is proper and surjective onto Yhat, its points are pencils of canonical divisors whose base divisor contains Gamma, the residual base-point-free pencil has degree k in (2,3,4), and dim D_k <= 15, 16, 17 respectively, whence dim D <= 17, dim Yhat <= 17 and dim Y <= 17; (5) therefore every admissible chain for Y has n_0 = dim Y <= 17, its top graded piece vanishes, and T_Z is noncanonically the direct sum of the graded pieces with 8 <= n_j <= 16. The bound in (4) is obtained entirely inside M_{6,6}, without an atlas of Hbar^bal, a twisted invertible sheaf, a Brauer class, or a PGL_2-quotient count, hence independently of both repairs FND-0187 leaves unwritten; FND-0194 records that no verified artifact previously computed it. parsed_artifact.theorem_statement: Let T_Z be the canonical mixed-Hodge subquotient of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) supplied by a verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum, and take as given the support filtration of a verified C66-SUPPORT-FILTRATION result: an admissible chain for Y, and a finite filtration of T_Z by sub-Hodge structures whose graded pieces are indexed by the stratum dimensions n of that chain, each a subquotient of W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q)(n), zero for n <= 7 and for n >= 17, a finite direct sum of Q(8) for n = 8, and at most one per dimension, so that at most eight pieces remain, at most one for each n with 9 <= n <= 16. Prove T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8). By the verified implication of that filtration it is sufficient to fix one admissible chain and prove, for each of its strata of dimension n with 9 <= n <= 16, that the corresponding graded piece is a finite direct sum of Q(8), for instance by determining W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) or by proving that the graded piece vanishes; any other complete proof of the displayed conclusion is equally admissible. A disproof must exhibit a non-Tate subquotient of this named T_Z through the verified target interface; non-Tate cohomology of an arbitrary family base, atlas, product model, standalone Z, or a source class whose target image is not proved nonzero is not a disproof, and neither is a non-Tate group W_{2n-16}H^{2n-16}(S_{(n)};Q) unless the corresponding graded piece of the verified filtration is itself proved non-Tate. This theorem does not itself assemble the complementary target terms.
